- Bringing OTP validation to the app makes pickup/delivery/return safer without disrupting the delivery person's workflow.

- Legacy removal + E2E QA — single path (validate → change status), with regression on dropoff and end-to-end QA in beta.

Finish developing Phase 1 of the "OTP" and begin developing Phase 3 of the MM (shipper photo log).

Main deliveries
- OTP Validation — Delivery Validation via Code: Implements OTP validation in the pickup stages, with a unified architecture (Lambda + MySQL).
- Middle Mile Phase 3 — Driver's Journey: It covers onboarding of the new process, recording of arrival evidence (arrival at pickup and dropoff), "arrive 10 min early" mode, evidence of loaded vehicle (photo sections categorized and error/recovery statuses per stage.
- Courier API v4 — Endpoint Migration: Continuation of migration to v4: migration of the registration endpoint and progress tracking document. Status: in progress. Important because it forms the basis for other features.

Sprint Constraints
Normal sprint, no holidays and no breaks with the developers.
However, it has already been highlighted that developer Patrick will be going on vacation in the middle of sprint 4, returning halfway through sprint 5.

Risks
No risks foreseen in this sprint.

Validations
No stakeholder validation occurred during sprint 3.
But it's worth highlighting that in Sprint 4 we will have the delivery of the shipper's photo stream for MM phase 3.

customfield_10020.name: Sprint 1
customfield_10020.goal:
Sprint Goal
Reduce operational risk and improve visibility of Slots

Main deliveries
- Re-enable Save Filters and fix filter persistence and presentation.
- Implement a notification panel for slots without assigned drivers.
- Improvements in Slot Detail: show Slot ID / Coverage ID / Shift ID, fix map fitBounds, and add a legend for driver color states.
- Operational rules and validations: block creation of slots for past shifts, prohibit Zipcode Ranges with slotsEnabled = true, and apply restrictions on edit/move/delete based on slot state and proximity to shift start.

Technical support:
We need to be available for any support team tickets, QA cards, and cards that may come from other squads during this transition period.

Sprint Constraints
May 25th is a holiday for the team that is outside of Brazil. 

Risks
No identified risks related to the Slots project. Monitor for possible intrusions from Middle Mile / Control Tower topics.

Validations
Validate the final delivery with Naiara Domingues and the Operations team, and monitor for potential improvements after release.

customfield_10020.name: Sprint 2
customfield_10020.goal:
Sprint Goal
- Bringing OTP validation to the app makes pickup/delivery/return safer without disrupting the delivery person's workflow.
Main deliveries
- OTP screen + gating — code entry screen (6 digits, loading/error, i18n es/en/pt), displayed only when the timeline marks the action as active: true.
- Validation before status change — integration with POST /v3/otp/validate; the status only advances in case of success, with error and retry in case of failure.
- Resend with cooldown + "no code" flow — POST /v3/otp/resend with button blocked during cooldown, and alternative path when the client does not have the code.
- Legacy removal + E2E QA — single path (validate → change status), with regression on dropoff and end-to-end QA in beta.

Sprint Constraints -> June 4th will be a holiday in Brazil.
Risks -> No risks foreseen in this sprint.
Validations -> No stakeholder validation occurred during sprint 2.

customfield_10020.name: Sprint 8
customfield_10020.goal:
Sprint Goal:

Close out Phase 3 of Control Tower by shipping the full filtering suite (Operation Type, Shipper/Client, Active Alert, Date, Lanes), the multi-stop trip navigation (Table, QuickView, and Trip Detail), and trip-list pagination — consolidating the Middle Mile monitoring foundation ahead of the final polish phase before the September delivery.

The 5 fronts that spanned all of Phase 3:

Alerts & Act Now (real-time prioritization and action queue) — from the initial Exception Control Tower concept through real-time alert delivery and UI severity coding.
KPI Header — the executive metrics bar, from initial UI/endpoint work through SLA Day and Cost/KM cards.
Multi-Stop Journey & Trip Detail — the evolution from single-delivery views to a full-route experience across the trips table, quick view, and trip detail page.
Global & Advanced Filters — from the original filtering discovery to the complete filter suite (Operation Type, Shipper, Active Alert, Date, Lanes, Saved Filters).
Data Foundation — the backend layer (lane persistence, ETA/SLA, alert case schema, pagination) underpinning the other four fronts.

customfield_10020.name: Sprint 7
customfield_10020.goal:
Sprint Goal

Close out the Control Tower (Torre de Controle) foundations already in flight — KPI header, structured alert tratativa and persisted destination ETA — and open the usability layer that makes the Tower workable at real operating volume: global filters, the lane as a queryable field, expandable multi-stop trips, quick view and a standardized alert catalog. In parallel, clear a batch of client-facing fixes with direct billing, SLA and legal exposure.

Product and UX/UI

Discovery — Global filters: client, date, lane, status, alert category (OE-301). Highest priority agreed for this sprint: without filters the Tower still shows the whole history at once.
Discovery — Expand a trip row into its deliveries and pickups (OE-304), ending the flattened duplicate rows in the trips list.
Quick view popup — journey, steps, evidence and event log (OE-302).

Main Deliveries

Alert Type Catalog — alert_type table plus the 15 seed records with translated labels and the external reference code (OE-296).
Persist the Amazon lane in a dedicated queryable field instead of a tag (OE-303) — prerequisite for the lane filter and for any per-lane analysis.
Act Now — structured tratativa reasons, operator ↔ driver (OE-220) + backend cadastro and persistence (OE-279).
Control Tower KPI header — Backend (OE-273) and Frontend (OE-232).

Progress (carried over from Sprint 6)

KPI header, BE (OE-273) and FE (OE-232) — Code Review
Act Now tratativa, FE (OE-220) — Code Review · BE (OE-279) — Waiting for tasks
Persist/display destination ETA via price_detail, owned by INF (OE-203) — In Progress
Vehicle assignment duplicate-plate filter (OE-191) — Rejected by QA, needs rework ⚠️

Must Be Completed This Sprint

KPI header end to end (OE-273 + OE-232) — third sprint in flight, cannot slip again
Alert tratativa end to end (OE-220 + OE-279)
ETA persistence via price_detail (OE-203)
Lane persisted in its own field (OE-303) — unblocks the global filter work

Also In This Sprint (client-facing fixes / maintenance / tech debt)

Return-task quota showing the wrong company, with invoice price divergence (OE-221). Incidence images and PDFs not reaching the driver app (OE-299). Package-size translation breaking the vehicle allocation rule (OE-295). Boticário account rename, VD ↔ OMNI inverted (OE-294). New "H2H" operation type and Middle Mile — Especiais rename (OE-249). Child-company selector in Import for basic parent accounts (OE-198). shippify.cl typography migration from Brother 1816 to Geologica, closing the licensing exposure (OE-293). Tech support (OE-343). Trainings and ceremonies (OE-314).

customfield_10020.name: Sprint 7
customfield_10020.goal:
Sprint Goal

Close out the Control Tower (Torre de Controle) foundations already in flight — KPI header, structured alert tratativa and persisted destination ETA — and open the usability layer that makes the Tower workable at real operating volume: global filters, the lane as a queryable field, expandable multi-stop trips, quick view and a standardized alert catalog. In parallel, clear a batch of client-facing fixes with direct billing, SLA and legal exposure.

Product and UX/UI

Discovery — Global filters: client, date, lane, status, alert category (OE-301). Highest priority agreed for this sprint: without filters the Tower still shows the whole history at once.
Discovery — Expand a trip row into its deliveries and pickups (OE-304), ending the flattened duplicate rows in the trips list.
Quick view popup — journey, steps, evidence and event log (OE-302).

Main Deliveries

Alert Type Catalog — alert_type table plus the 15 seed records with translated labels and the external reference code (OE-296).
Persist the Amazon lane in a dedicated queryable field instead of a tag (OE-303) — prerequisite for the lane filter and for any per-lane analysis.
Act Now — structured tratativa reasons, operator ↔ driver (OE-220) + backend cadastro and persistence (OE-279).
Control Tower KPI header — Backend (OE-273) and Frontend (OE-232).

Progress (carried over from Sprint 6)

KPI header, BE (OE-273) and FE (OE-232) — Code Review
Act Now tratativa, FE (OE-220) — Code Review · BE (OE-279) — Waiting for tasks
Persist/display destination ETA via price_detail, owned by INF (OE-203) — In Progress
Vehicle assignment duplicate-plate filter (OE-191) — Rejected by QA, needs rework ⚠️

Must Be Completed This Sprint

KPI header end to end (OE-273 + OE-232) — third sprint in flight, cannot slip again
Alert tratativa end to end (OE-220 + OE-279)
ETA persistence via price_detail (OE-203)
Lane persisted in its own field (OE-303) — unblocks the global filter work

Also In This Sprint (client-facing fixes / maintenance / tech debt)

Return-task quota showing the wrong company, with invoice price divergence (OE-221). Incidence images and PDFs not reaching the driver app (OE-299). Package-size translation breaking the vehicle allocation rule (OE-295). Boticário account rename, VD ↔ OMNI inverted (OE-294). New "H2H" operation type and Middle Mile — Especiais rename (OE-249). Child-company selector in Import for basic parent accounts (OE-198). shippify.cl typography migration from Brother 1816 to Geologica, closing the licensing exposure (OE-293). Tech support (OE-343). Trainings and ceremonies (OE-314).

customfield_10020.goal:
Sprint Goal
- Standardize the dashboard on shared platform components and bring real-time visibility to the Smart Notification driver-rotation process.

Main deliveries
- Real-time visibility of Smart Notifications — propagate data to Firebase (userId, slotId/deliverySlotId, round), extend the RealTimeProgress widget to the smart notification collection, display jobs in the Slots header, and redesign the card in Route Detail.

- Migration of the Companies page to React — wiring of the route/bundle, table with server-side pagination, and search bar with debounce, moving away from EJS/jQuery.

June 4th will be a holiday in Brazil.

No risks foreseen in this sprint.

customfield_10020.name: Sprint 6
customfield_10020.goal:
Sprint Goal

Objective – Sprint Goal
Continue building the Torre de Controle (Control Tower) for Middle Mile: add the KPI header so operation health is visible at a glance (trips, in-route, delayed, Act Now, SLA, cost/km), formalize how operators resolve alerts with structured, auditable reasons, and roll out the finalized UI layout across the Control Tower's core screens. The real-time Act Now alerts panel carried over from Sprint 5 is now blocked and needs to be unblocked to avoid slipping a second sprint.

Product and UX/UI

FE layout updates on the Control Tower Main Page (OE-239), Act Now (OE-240) and Trip Detail (OE-241), per finalized Figma — To Do
Evaluation: unify the basic-company "comment" modal with the incidences modal (OE-247) — In Progress

Main Deliveries

Control Tower KPI header — Backend (OE-273) and Frontend (OE-232) — To Do
Act Now — structured tratativa (resolution) reasons, operator↔driver (OE-220) + backend persistence (OE-279) — To Do

Progress (carried over from Sprint 5)

Persist/display destination ETA via price_detail, owned by INF (OE-203) — In Progress
Act Now panel — real-time alert updates via session channels (OE-202) — Blocked ⚠️

Must Be Completed This Sprint

Unblock and ship the Act Now real-time alerts panel (OE-202)
ETA persistence via price_detail (OE-203)
KPI header, backend + frontend (OE-273, OE-232)

Also In This Sprint (maintenance / tech debt)
Reserved-points tech support (OE-290) and Import Edit Address UX (OE-197) — To Do. Vehicle assignment duplicate-plate filter fix (OE-191) — Code Review. RCD-TECHLOG order date issue (OE-93) — Rejected by QA, needs rework. Monthly planning & retrospective ceremony (OE-250).

Continue building the Torre de Controle (Control Tower) for Middle Mile: add the KPI header so operation health is visible at a glance (trips, in-route, delayed, Act Now, SLA, cost/km), formalize how operators resolve alerts with structured, auditable reasons, and roll out the finalized UI layout across the Control Tower's core screens. The real-time Act Now alerts panel carried over from Sprint 5 is now blocked and needs to be unblocked to avoid slipping a second sprint.

FE layout updates on the Control Tower Main Page (OE-239), Act Now (OE-240) and Trip Detail (OE-241), per finalized Figma — To Do

Control Tower KPI header — Backend (OE-273) and Frontend (OE-232) — To Do
Act Now — structured tratativa (resolution) reasons, operator↔driver (OE-220) + backend persistence (OE-279) — To Do

Progress (carried over from Sprint 5)

Persist/display destination ETA via price_detail, owned by INF (OE-203) — In Progress
Act Now panel — real-time alert updates via session channels (OE-202) — Blocked ⚠️

Must Be Completed This Sprint

Unblock and ship the Act Now real-time alerts panel (OE-202)
ETA persistence via price_detail (OE-203)
KPI header, backend + frontend (OE-273, OE-232)

Reserved-points tech support (OE-290) and Import Edit Address UX (OE-197) — To Do. Vehicle assignment duplicate-plate filter fix (OE-191) — Code Review. RCD-TECHLOG order date issue (OE-93) — Rejected by QA, needs rework. Monthly planning & retrospective ceremony (OE-250).

Complete the migration of drivers active since 2025 (~90K) on Fleet, executed in batches to avoid impacting system stability.
Ship and validate the Fleet payment-data filter (drivers missing CPF/Pix key) for the Operations team.

Link and resolve the Abiamo/Americanas cancellation status sync under the existing integration ticket (EE-3).
Continue migrating integration documentation from Notion to Confluence (PROD-243).
Deliver the Dash Control Tower percentage metrics requested by the Operations team (EE-397).
Maintain capacity for Tech Support demands without compromising the planned backlog.

Fleet migration of 2025 drivers cohort completed and validated.
Flit onboarding documentation (EE-393) finalized with architectural improvement recommendations.
TOTVS payment reprocessing subtasks scoped, aligned with Gustavo, and in progress.
Dash Control Tower metrics delivered to support Operations' rollout.

Sprint Constraints

We have a holiday in Brazil on September 7th, reducing the team's available capacity by one day for this sprint.

Risks

We do not foresee any risk of version updates in this sprint.

Validations

Validation with Gustavo regarding TOTVS payment reprocessing scoring, and with the Operations team regarding Dash Control Tower metrics.

fields.summary: Migrate EDSP pipeline to module-gamification - Sprint 7

customfield_10020.name: EE Sprint 7
customfield_10020.goal:
Sprint Goal
Execute the CDN bucket privatization across all affected integration points (the largest block of the sprint), advance the two structural Fleet initiatives — gradual migration of ~65,000 drivers and standardization of payment configuration — deliver visibility into TOTVS transaction sync status, and kick off the Datadog observability POC.

Main Deliveries
CDN Bucket Privatization (30 pts) — EE-276, EE-277 (+ subtasks Sequoia, Unacem, novoTracking, Falabella), EE-282, EE-283, EE-284, EE-285: update lambda-actions, lambda-functions, Shippify-Server, and Shippify-Server-Lambda to stop relying on public bucket URLs.
Fleet — Driver Migration (4 pts) — EE-308: alerts, monitoring, and execution support for the gradual Lambda-based migration of ~65,000 drivers.
Fleet — Payment Standardization (4 pts) — EE-312: map the mandatory payment configuration requirements at driver registration.
TOTVS — Sync Status (8 pts) — EE-351: sync status field on bill transactions, reconciliation lambda, and automated Slack report.
Tech Support & Bugs (19 pts) — EE-334, EE-335: support containers.
Observability (8 pts) — EE-347: Datadog POC for squad monitoring.
Integration (3 pts) — EE-332: integration ADR.
Sustainability (5 pts) — EE-356 (TypeScript/cleanup) and EE-357 (migrate the EDSP pipeline to the Gamification module).

Total committed: ~89 pts

Sprint Constraints
No holidays expected during the sprint window (08/11–08/26).

Risks
CDN Bucket Privatization has a large change surface (6 different systems) and depends on external partners (Unacem, Falabella) not breaking on privatization day.
EE-347 (Datadog) is an exploratory POC — scope may shift based on findings.

Vacation of Sairys, who is responsible for shared QA during the final part of the sprint from August 17 to August 21. Return is expected on August 24, considering the two weekend days, which is the last day of the sprint.

customfield_10020.name: EE Sprint 6
customfield_10020.goal:
Sprint Goal:

Balance the squad's strategic pillars — IDwall, Fleet, Gamification, and TOTVS/Integration — keeping the sprint lean and allowing continuous refinement on the areas of highest current focus: Fleet and IDwall.

Main Deliveries
IDwall — EE-235 (4 pts): Registration failure caused by CPF length validation — bug fix that may be artificially inflating the error rate in the registration flow.
Fleet — EE-254 (8 pts): Phone number format validation for driver registration. EE-231 (8 pts): Fix phone number update flow in the app, prerequisite for the upcoming communication campaign. EE-238 (9 pts): Review and understanding, preparation for driver migration.
Gamification — EE-186 (5 pts): Review and fix Gamification UI (carried over from Sprint 5).
TOTVS/Integration — EE-237 (7 pts): ADR formalizing the request → ADR → prioritization → sprint flow.
Tech Support — EE-247, EE-248, EE-253 (7–13 pts each): consolidated low-effort support containers.

Sprint Constraints
Feriado Ecuador: segunda-feira, 10/08 é feriado nacional (Primer Grito de Independencia) — reduz a capacidade de José Cedeño na segunda semana da sprint (a sprint roda de 28/07 a 11/08).

customfield_10020.name: EE Sprint 7
customfield_10020.goal:
Sprint Goal
Execute the CDN bucket privatization across all affected integration points (the largest block of the sprint), advance the two structural Fleet initiatives — gradual migration of ~65,000 drivers and standardization of payment configuration — deliver visibility into TOTVS transaction sync status, and kick off the Datadog observability POC.

Main Deliveries
CDN Bucket Privatization (30 pts) — EE-276, EE-277 (+ subtasks Sequoia, Unacem, novoTracking, Falabella), EE-282, EE-283, EE-284, EE-285: update lambda-actions, lambda-functions, Shippify-Server, and Shippify-Server-Lambda to stop relying on public bucket URLs.
Fleet — Driver Migration (4 pts) — EE-308: alerts, monitoring, and execution support for the gradual Lambda-based migration of ~65,000 drivers.
Fleet — Payment Standardization (4 pts) — EE-312: map the mandatory payment configuration requirements at driver registration.
TOTVS — Sync Status (8 pts) — EE-351: sync status field on bill transactions, reconciliation lambda, and automated Slack report.
Tech Support & Bugs (19 pts) — EE-334, EE-335: support containers.
Observability (8 pts) — EE-347: Datadog POC for squad monitoring.
Integration (3 pts) — EE-332: integration ADR.
Sustainability (5 pts) — EE-356 (TypeScript/cleanup) and EE-357 (migrate the EDSP pipeline to the Gamification module).

Total committed: ~89 pts

Sprint Constraints
No holidays expected during the sprint window (08/11–08/26).

CDN Bucket Privatization has a large change surface (6 different systems) and depends on external partners (Unacem, Falabella) not breaking on privatization day.

customfield_10020.name: EE Sprint 6
customfield_10020.goal:
Sprint Goal:

Balance the squad's strategic pillars — IDwall, Fleet, Gamification, and TOTVS/Integration — keeping the sprint lean and allowing continuous refinement on the areas of highest current focus: Fleet and IDwall.

Main Deliveries
IDwall — EE-235 (4 pts): Registration failure caused by CPF length validation — bug fix that may be artificially inflating the error rate in the registration flow.
Fleet — EE-254 (8 pts): Phone number format validation for driver registration. EE-231 (8 pts): Fix phone number update flow in the app, prerequisite for the upcoming communication campaign. EE-238 (9 pts): Review and understanding, preparation for driver migration.
Gamification — EE-186 (5 pts): Review and fix Gamification UI (carried over from Sprint 5).
TOTVS/Integration — EE-237 (7 pts): ADR formalizing the request → ADR → prioritization → sprint flow.
Tech Support — EE-247, EE-248, EE-253 (7–13 pts each): consolidated low-effort support containers.

Sprint Constraints
Feriado Ecuador: segunda-feira, 10/08 é feriado nacional (Primer Grito de Independencia) — reduz a capacidade de José Cedeño na segunda semana da sprint (a sprint roda de 28/07 a 11/08).
Nenhum feriado em São Paulo durante o período da sprint.

Risks
Investigação de CPF (EE-235) pode revelar impacto maior do que o estimado nas validações de cadastro do IDwall.
Validations
Sprint validations conducted by the Communities, Operations, and Finance teams.

customfield_10020.goal:
Sprint Goal
Reduce operational risk and improve visibility of Slots

Main deliveries
- Re-enable Save Filters and fix filter persistence and presentation.
- Implement a notification panel for slots without assigned drivers.
- Improvements in Slot Detail: show Slot ID / Coverage ID / Shift ID, fix map fitBounds, and add a legend for driver color states.
- Operational rules and validations: block creation of slots for past shifts, prohibit Zipcode Ranges with slotsEnabled = true, and apply restrictions on edit/move/delete based on slot state and proximity to shift start.

Technical support:
We need to be available for any support team tickets, QA cards, and cards that may come from other squads during this transition period.

Sprint Constraints
May 25th is a holiday for the team that is outside of Brazil. 

Risks
No identified risks related to the Slots project. Monitor for possible intrusions from Middle Mile / Control Tower topics.

Validations
Validate the final delivery with Naiara Domingues and the Operations team, and monitor for potential improvements after release.
